name: pareto-two-objectives
description: Two-objective MAB with a concave part in its Pareto front (as in Drugan and Nowe, 2013), Gaussian noise 0.2, 20 runs. Regret of the 0.5 / 0.5 scalarization and Pareto measures.

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Values of the papers: ParetoUCB1 alpha=1, UCB1 alpha=1. They give the theoretical confidence bounds: safe in theory, but they often explore too much in practice. To fit them to this problem, run a grid search (param_grid=True, or "param_grid": true in a config file) or set them, e.g. ParetoUCB1(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Assumed constants
notices.text: The environment does not give them: reward_range: b=1 (unknown for this problem) for ParetoUCB1 and UCB1. Pass the true values to the policies if you know them (help(policy) lists the parameters).

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret (track "pseudo_regret"); reward per objective (track "reward_vec"); per-action estimates (track "estimates"); action of every step (track "actions"). The dashboard and the figures cannot show what is not stored; the brackets say how to store it (in a config file: "track": [...] or "measure_memory": true in "experiment").

notices.title: One point every 50 steps
notices.text: Curves keep one point every 50 steps and the last step (log_interval=50). The values at these points are exact. Between two points, the charts draw a straight line: there the curve is interpolated, not measured. log_interval=1 keeps every step (larger files).

notices.title: Slower timings
notices.text: measure_memory=True slows Python code about fivefold: compare CPU times only between runs with the same setting.

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: With n_jobs=4, each process uses one BLAS thread: compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
